rngtwt: This week you review two classes that share pronouns: verbs like **gustar** (_interesar, doler, faltar, molestar_), where the verb agrees with the thing, and the **indirect object** (_me, te, le, nos, les_) with verbs like _dar, mandar, decir_. Here you use them shopping around Suchitoto, among indigo workshops and sore feet.
10v236h: Gustar the other way round: the verb looks at the thing
96hyom: With **gustar**, the person is not the subject. The subject is **what is liked**, and the verb agrees with it: _me gusta **el mercado**_ (one thing), _me gustan **los mercados**_ (several things). The person appears as a pronoun: **me, te, le, nos, os, les**.
mhpi1a: They go in the **singular** (_gusta_): one thing, something uncountable (_el café, la música_) and infinitives, one or several (_me gusta caminar y nadar_). They go in the **plural** (_gustan_): a plural noun or two things together (_me gustan el café y el chocolate_).
m4cdd5: **Interesar**, **encantar** and **molestar** work the same way: _nos interesa la historia_, _les encantan las hamacas_, _me molesta el ruido_.
ivtfm2: The person goes with a pronoun (**me**) and the verb agrees with _los mercados_: **gustan**.
thn6ms: With infinitives, always **gusta**, even if there are two.
mc54yt: Doler, faltar, molestar: the same pattern
1pn5vgk: **Doler** follows the pattern of gustar: _me duele **la cabeza**_, _me duelen **los pies**_. With body parts you use the article (**la** cabeza), not the possessive: _me duele la espalda_, not _mi espalda_.
6fte7j: **Faltar** says something isn't there or isn't enough: _me falta **dinero**_, _nos faltan **dos boletos**_. It is also used without a person for what's left: _faltan **cuatro horas** para el bus_. Compare: _necesito tiempo_ (I am the subject) and _me falta tiempo_ (time is the subject).
13dshn0: In the past the agreement doesn't change: _me dolió la rodilla_, _me dolieron las piernas_; _nos gustó el taller_, _nos gustaron las tazas_.
10u1820: Before conjugating, ask yourself: what is liked, what hurts, what is missing? That word decides whether the verb is singular or plural.
kgcmzh: With the body, use the article: **la** cabeza. The _me_ already says whose it is.
1kptj7c: A mí, a ti, a Laura: clarifying and insisting
z7vtb1: You can add **a + person** to make clear who it is (_le gusta_ could be he, she or you: **a Laura** le gusta) or to insist, especially when comparing: _A mí me encanta el picante, pero a mi hermano no_.
5lcwn7: Even if you say _a Laura_ or _a mí_, the pronoun **doesn't disappear**: _A Laura le gusta_, never _A Laura gusta_.
1vue5iq: To react to someone else's taste: **a mí también** (same as me, with yes), **a mí tampoco** (same as me, with no), **a mí sí** and **a mí no** (I'm different).
1lppwqo: With _a mis primos_ you also need **les**.
hao43d: To whom? Me, te, le, nos, les with dar, mandar, decir
1j83mb7: The **indirect object** says **to whom** or **for whom** an action is: _le regalé un pañuelo_ (to my mother). You use it with verbs of giving and communicating: _dar, regalar, prestar, traer, mandar, escribir, decir, preguntar, contestar, explicar_.
10dttqj: It goes before the conjugated verb: _te mando las fotos_, _nos explicó el proceso_. With **le** and **les** it's very common to repeat the person afterwards: _Le di las gracias **a la artesana**_. If the person goes in front, or if you say _a mí, a ti, a él…_, the pronoun is compulsory: _A la artesana le di las gracias_.
1khvaki: Don't confuse it with **lo, la, los, las**, which answer _what?_ or _whom?_ with verbs like _ver, llamar, invitar_: _la llamé_ (Marta), but _le dije la hora_ (to Marta). To recognise: in parts of Spain some people say _le vi_ for a man; it's a variant the RAE accepts.
vtfba6: Ask the question: **to whom** do I give, say or send something? If the answer is a person who receives, use **le / les**.

1majja0: The -n that changes everything: duele / duelen
1ajnq8t: Between _me duele el pie_ and _me duelen los pies_ the difference is an **n** at the end of the verb. It's small, but it changes the agreement.
q2h9rz: When the next word starts with a vowel, the **n** joins it and is easier to hear: _me gustan_estas tazas_ sounds like _gus-ta-nes-tas_. When a consonant follows, you have to mark it a little: _me gustan los collares_.
1opv5na: Another clue: the article. _El, la_ and _este_ go with **-a/-e**; _los, las_ and _estos_ go with **-an/-en**.
1b7azn4: **Mí** with an accent is the pronoun (_a mí me gusta_); **mi** without an accent is the possessive (_mi madre_). The same with **tú** (_¿y tú?_) and **tu** (_tu regalo_).
